questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A school with a good reputation and a nice mix between Canadian culture and the more American culture. Many sports teams as well (hockey, basketball, baseball etc.)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. Most places offer leases/contracts for an entire year, and one semester stays are very expensive. I would recommend applying for a place in Tartu (if you prefer a few roommates) early before all spots are taken, or Coop Housing (if you prefer to live with many different people).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to live with someone attending the same university, you should make sure that the place is not located closer to another university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university almost only offers places to live for longer term stays and do not prioritize exchange students. The spots you can find once you are accepted are very limited.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite annoying that they provide zero information on the actual syllabus and when they hold midterm tests and exams when you register (they announce midterms after you start, and exams are announced in the end of October...)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive an email with a google form you need to fill out with the courses you wish to take. They do multiple rounds of these, so you can decide pretty late what courses to take, though they need to be approved of course. Also, you can drop and take new courses a few weeks into the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a page where you can look at what course combinations are feasible and how your schedule looks.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all four of mine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Accept that you do not know for sure what the courses are about and the important dates. Other than that, just find some courses which you think resemble courses you could take back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is definitely lower, but you can feel that they previously have been focusing on other things, because at some points you felt slightly behind and at other points you felt way ahead. The professors were mostly very good, but the teaching assistants were not the best at helping with the types of problems you would be required to solve.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is quite similar, although the weekly exercises at UCPH are way more rewarding.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECO310 - Empirical Industrial Organization
ECO313 - Environmental Economics and Policies
ECO314 - Energy and the Environment
ECO324 - Economic Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend ECO314, if you're interested in the environment and how it is related to economics and geopolitics. If you like some light STATA work, then ECO310 is a good choice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Things as mandatory health insurance at the university, which made no sense. And also getting used to tips and taxes at restaurants etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices on different groceries are very different. But generally food is quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can join an endless amount of clubs - there's something for everyone. Gym access and tickets for the university team sports games are free for students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to a Raptors, Maple Leafs or Blue Jays game, a very different experience compared to sports games back home. Also, go to Niagara Falls.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a trip to Algonquin, Montreal, or Banff.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. But get used to the fact that people attending university in Toronto are very young.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend going to one of the club activities. If you like running, then the run club (UTRC) is a good place to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, but get used to big cars and limited biking options.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like some of the sports culture (primarily the fact that the level of the hockey and basketball are so much higher than back home), and the people in Toronto (and Canada in general) are mostly very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply early for housing. The people I spoke to that stayed at Tartu enjoyed that, and it's not too expensive.
2. Go to some of the activities that people suggest (you can get added to a big whatsapp group chat with every exchange student at UofT). That's how I met almost all the people I was with.
3. Focus on doing well at your midterm tests. You only need 50% to pass the course, and the exam schedule in December (for fall semester) can be very tight, so if you prioritize some of the early opportunities to score points you can enjoy the last weeks of your stay way more.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really. But I would say that you shouldn't focus too much on school and enjoy the city. You generally receive pretty high grades, so even though you fear that you are gonna fail, it will be alright if you put in just some effort.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing what studying at a completely different university feels like, and meeting some very nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At some points, it was a little tough that you weren't able to see friends and family from home, but luckily I found some nice people to hang out with over there and a semester is not that long.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
